text:
sanjay r: Quick sync — OpenScene sent a tarball of weights and says they're 'community-clean'. Before we approve a marketplace listing we need proof of origin + clear redistribution terms. Any immediate red flags?

megan (partnerships): Do we have the repo/source commits and the training-data provenance? If not, ask them for SBoM and commit hashes. Also need a signed attestation from the provider. :eyes:

kate (legal): Short answer: we need a signed vendor attestation + license compatibility review. If weights reference code/models under Apache/MIT that's generally okay, but any CC-BY/SA or restricted dataset provenance will complicate redistribution. Also export-control: origin country and contributors matter.

liam (product): From a risk POV, we should gate the listing behind a canary distribution (Dedicated pool only) and a short SLA that limits how aggressively it can be promoted until legal/ops clear it. We can use existing rollout controls.

olivia (marketplace): For listing metadata we'll need: model size, quantization variants, throughput benchmarks, example prompts, suggested pricing, and a contact for vulnerability reports. If redistribution is allowed, we need explicit allowed channels (marketplace, enterprise offers, partners).

megan (partnerships): I've pinged OpenScene to provide: repo link + commit hashes, dataset manifest, signed attestation, and confirmation of any 3rd party licenses used. ETA EOW.

kate (legal): Draft checklist (quick):

```
- Signed provider attestation (proof of origin + contributor list)
- Source repo + commit hashes and build instructions
- License compatibility matrix (code, model, datasets)
- Export-control self-assessment (origin country, contributors)
- Indemnity / liability carveouts for third-party claims
- Redistribution scope (allowed/disallowed channels)
- Required attribution text
```

kate (legal): Proposed contract language excerpt for redistribution rights (very rough):

`Provider hereby grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide license to distribute, reproduce, and offer the Model to Redwood's customers via Redwood's hosted, dedicated, and private deployment channels, subject to the restrictions set forth in Section X (Redistribution Restrictions). Provider retains ownership of the Model and warrants that it has the right to grant these rights.`

kate (legal): Note — provider asked for 'unrestricted redistribution'. We should push back on indefinite onward redistribution to 3rd-party marketplaces; require prior written consent.

megan (partnerships): Agree. If OpenScene insists on permissive terms we can offer a tiered approach: marketplace listing + telemetry requirement for 30 days, then broader redistribution if no claims.

legal-bot: POLICY_CHECK: origin-signature missing — flagged HIGH. Please obtain cryptographic proof of origin (commit signature or GPG-signed release) per internal policy.

liam (product): Can ops enforce a quick rollback trigger? If we detect a takedown/claim we should be able to delist within X hours automatically. I'll add a canary + auto-revert in the deployment plan.

olivia (marketplace): Also: marketing/announcement coordination — we must not publish a joint blog until legal confirms redistribution scope and export controls. If OpenScene wants a co-announcement, we need 2-week lead and pre-approved copy.

sanjay r: Action items recap: (1) Megan to get attestation + repo + SBoM from OpenScene (ETA EOW). (2) Kate to draft attestation template + propose redistribution clause (ETA 48h). (3) Liam to prepare canary rollout + auto-revert plan. (4) Olivia to draft listing metadata template and announcement gating checklist. I'll schedule a 30-min call with OpenScene + Legal for tomorrow 10:00 PT.

megan (partnerships): On it. Adding items to the partnerships board and will link the OpenScene PR once received.

kate (legal): I'll post the attestation template in that board and add a short FAQ on common license pitfalls.

liam (product): I'll add the canary config snippet to the deployment doc. Example rollback trigger: `if(resolution=="takedown" || legal_claims>0) auto_revert()` — will formalize.

olivia (marketplace): Noted. If we get the attestation + signed commits we can tentatively schedule listing review next Wed.

sanjay r: Thanks everyone. tagging: @kate (legal) @megan (partnerships) @olivia (marketplace) — please update this thread when you have the doc links. :thumbsup:
